It pins today's **defective** behaviour and says so in its own comment. ⚠️ **Repairing the defect will turn that probe red, and that is correct** — the probe is where the fix lands, ⛔ not an obstacle to it. Rewrite it to assert the repaired behaviour and keep its comment honest about what changed.

## The defect, already measured to source level by triage — ⛔ re-take it, do not inherit it

`:492` opens `if (meta?.namespace && !meta?.skipFallback) {`; `:506`'s bare-key claim is **inside** that branch; `:511` closes it; and `:515` / `:516`'s `this.lazyEntries.delete(...)` sit at **function-body level, unconditional**.

⇒ with `skipFallback: true`, `:506` never runs and `:516` runs anyway ⇒ **the registration neither claims the bare key nor leaves it with its owner.** The bare key ends up claimed by nobody.

⚠️ Those line numbers were taken **before** objectui#9838 landed 83 lines into this same file. **Re-take every one of them** on a freshly fetched `origin/main` and report the ref and UTC time. ⛔ Do not cite a line number this card's body prints.

## ⭐ FIRST TASK — triage's escalation condition, and it asks about the SOURCE

Triage's escalation clause, verbatim: 「⭐ 该条件同时问**来源**:若测到有文档或示例在教人用 `skipFallback: true` 去「避免影响别人」,同样升级 —— **那句话正在制造受害者**。」

⇒ **before writing the fix, sweep for teaching that prescribes `skipFallback: true` as a way to avoid clobbering another declaration** — `content/docs/**`, `skills/**`, package READMEs, JSDoc, changesets, and ⚠️ `Registry.ts`'s own existing warning strings, one of which literally prescribes it. Report what you find with the file and line.

If such teaching exists, say so plainly in the report: **this card escalates to `priority:p1` and that is triage's call, ⛔ not yours and ⛔ not mine.** Keep building either way — the escalation changes the grade, ⛔ not the fix.

## ⚠️ SECOND face, measured by this seat and ⛔ NOT by the filer or triage

`unregister` at `:530`–`:542` (pre-objectui#9838 numbering) carries the **same unconditional pair**:

- `:534`–`:536` guards the bare `components` key — `if (bare && bare.type === fullType) this.components.delete(type);` — it only drops it when it still resolves to this registration;
- `:538`–`:539` `this.lazyEntries.delete(fullType); this.lazyEntries.delete(type);` — **no equivalent guard**.

And its docblock at `:521`–`:523` says it clears 「the bare-name fallback (**when the fallback still points at this registration**), plus any **matching** lazy stub」.

⚠️ **Stated as a reading, ⛔ not as a verdict.** Whether `:539` is a defect turns on whether 「any **matching** lazy stub」 means 「a stub under either key」 or 「a stub that belongs to this registration」. ⇒ **Rule that phrase from the code's behaviour before choosing the fix shape**, because the two readings give two different patches. ⚠️ If `unregister` turns out to need the same repair, it is in this file and in scope; if the phrase legitimately means the looser thing, say so and leave `unregister` alone. ⛔ Do not fix it silently either way.

## ⚠️ Stop conditions

1. ⚠️ **If the repair changes which registrations are ACCEPTED** — rather than which bare key survives — stop and report. This card is about a `delete` that runs when it should not; it is ⛔ not a licence to change `skipFallback`'s contract.
2. ⚠️ **If making `:516` conditional turns any existing green test red other than the named probe**, stop and report the test by name before adapting it. A test that goes red is a claim about behaviour someone pinned on purpose; ⛔ it is not an obstacle to be edited away.

## Reading discipline

Every zero needs a same-subject control that fires **in the same command**. ⛔ Resolve refs before grepping (`git cat-file -t "$REF" >/dev/null || exit 1`). ⛔ Print LINES, never a bare count, when a count is the evidence. ⚠️ And this lane has measured **five** times in one shift that a code-shaped pattern gives a false zero *or a false count* against a regex literal, a loop variable, a `const` declaration, spacing, or non-code text inside a template string — the last one being an `<body>` HTML tag in a generated template. **Read the block.**

### ② ⭐⭐ `unregister` was ruled from BEHAVIOUR, not from the wording — and the ruling is right

The claim left the 「any **matching** lazy stub」 phrase to be ruled before the fix shape was chosen, because the two readings give two different patches. The delivery ruled it **ownership**, and the argument is the strongest sentence in this card:

> `unregister` already answers that question for the bare `components` key and answers it **ownership** — it will not drop bare `dashboard` when it resolves to `plugin-dashboard:dashboard`. Reading the next line as an unconditional delete makes the **SAME call, on the SAME bare key, with the SAME owner**, take the opposite decision purely because the owner happens to be sitting in the other table at that instant — and which table it is sitting in is exactly the 「has the chunk loaded yet」 race that objectui#9533 and objectui#9821 are about. **A policy that flips on chunk-load timing is not a policy.**

⭐ And it is not hypothetical: with `register` repaired and `unregister` left alone, the identical victim survives one function down.
